text: By the time the red emergency lights came on at the Ruvenna data centre on 17 April last spring, engineers were already hearing the first alarms from the eastern server hall. The cause, investigators confirmed this week, was a failed cooling pump in the facility’s primary circulation loop. With coolant flow cut to a fraction of normal, temperatures climbed within minutes and several racks shut down automatically. The outage lasted 3 hours and 42 minutes, briefly interrupting services for three municipal agencies and two private logistics firms. Ruvenna’s operator, Helix Mora Systems, said the pump had been installed in 2019 and was due for replacement later this year. For a complex built to withstand nearly everything, the failure was a reminder of how quickly one small component can still unsettle an entire digital district.
